messages:
rachel: odd bug in the Next + LangChain starter when a streaming tool call gets retried mid-flight — we see duplicated tool outputs (same snippet twice) in the final agent answer. anyone seen this?
tony: hmm. which starter + sdk versions?
rachel: devex-starters/langchain-agent-demo. Notebook uses redwood-py==0.8.2, the frontend demo uses @redwood/sdk-js==0.8.1. Repro: run the agent with a streaming 'web_cite' tool that emits 3 chunks, force a simulated intermittent 500 in the middle of the stream. The final assembled response contains chunk2 twice.
marta: can you paste the snippet and captured callback events?
rachel: snippet (simplified):
```python
# agent harness
resp = agent.run("Summarize and cite")  # agent uses web_cite tool streamed
# callbacks capture tool_stream chunks
```
captured events (sanitized):
```
tool_start(web_cite)
tool_stream(chunk1)
tool_stream(chunk2)
STREAM ERROR 500
SDK RETRY attempt=1 resubmit-tool-call
tool_start(web_cite)
tool_stream(chunk2)
tool_stream(chunk3)
tool_end(web_cite)
generation_end
```
As you can see chunk2 appears twice because the SDK retried the tool invocation without informing the agent harness to de-duplicate or close the prior tool span.
tony: yikes. That could break citation anchors or cause duplicated inserts in downstream databases. Is the SDK re-sending the entire tool call or only resuming?
rachel: it's re-sending the tool call from scratch. The JS SDK currently emits a 'tool_retry' event and wraps retries in a new tool span, and the devex harness correlator ignores duplicate tool spans by id. Python SDK lacks the 'tool_retry' event and reuses the same tool span id so the harness thinks the second sequence is a continuation.
marta: SDK parity gap then. Quick mitigations: 1) update the sample harness to normalize duplicate tool streams by checking content hashes and dropping exact duplicates; 2) patch the Python SDK to emit explicit tool_retry events and to generate a new tool span id when a retry occurs, matching JS behavior.
rachel: for workshops we need immediate relief — I've opened a PR to the starter that adds a lightweight dedupe pass in the notebook that collapses identical consecutive chunks before assembling the final answer. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex-starters/pull/1427
sdk-ops-bot: ISSUE-1428 created to implement tool_retry/span-id parity in python-sdk. Assigned to @tony.
tony: thanks. Plan: implement tool_retry event + new span id on retry in python-sdk. Also add telemetry counter `tool_retries` and a flag `sdk.retry_streaming_tools=true/false` default false for interactive clients. Will add unit tests to assert event ordering: tool_start, tool_stream*, (tool_retry, tool_start...), tool_end, generation_end.
qa-bot: adding an eval to eng-ml/nightly: stream-tool-retry-dedup that runs a mocked tool which emits 3 chunks, fails mid-stream (500), then succeeds on retry. The eval asserts the final callback sequence contains only one copy of each chunk when dedupe is enabled.
marta: long-term we should also add a higher-level pattern doc in the starter on how to design idempotent tools (tool ids, chunk checksums) so retries don't corrupt downstream state. I'll add a short section to the sample README w/ examples.
rachel: validated the notebook PR locally; dedupe patch prevents the visible duplicate in the assembled text but we still need the SDK change so callbacks and telemetry reflect retries properly.
tony: implementing SDK change now. I'll push a branch and request review. After that I'll cut a patch release and update the starter to bump the pinned SDK.
qa-bot: preview deploy for pr-1427 available: https://preview.redwood.dev/devex-starters/pr-1427 :rocket:
marta: also adding a short checklist for workshop slides: "use idempotent tools or enable SDK dedupe flag" to reduce confusion during demos.
rachel: great work team. once python-sdk patch lands we'll remove the temporary dedupe in the notebook and rely on consistent event ordering. leaving a note in the sample's README about the interim fix. :thumbsup:
